channel.title: Awesome Trustworthy Jev — Papers
channel.description: Jev research papers, ordered by first public publication date.

item.title: Radiology Guideline-derived Decision Graph for Efficient Clinical Decision Support
item.description: Compiles clinical guidelines into an executable decision graph, separates local Jev judgments from deterministic traversal, and reports higher accuracy than direct or retrieval-augmented inference on 347 cases.

item.title: When the Top Answer Decides: Gender Bias in Decision Models
item.description: Audits gender-swapped decisions, stereotypes and confidence gating in Jev and five open decision models. Probability preferences and top-answer changes differ; confidence filtering can increase the stereotyped share of retained ambiguous answers.

item.title: Decision and System One models in rheumatology: accuracy and calibration on specialty-training examination questions and diagnostic case vignettes
item.description: Compares decision models on examination questions and diagnostic vignettes. Jev’s high-confidence accuracy falls from 98.5% on examinations to 84.6% on selected vignettes, showing that confidence reliability does not transfer automatically across tasks.

item.title: FlipJev: Fast Black-Box Red Teaming Finds Universal Adversarial Suffixes for Typed Decision Models
item.description: Evaluates adaptive suffix attacks against a fixed Jev 1.13 snapshot. Dataset-specific universal suffixes flip 114/264 held-out confident positive decisions; cross-task transfer averages 18%, while a selected suffix reaches 90–100% on five tasks.

item.title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents
item.description: Learns direct program-pair selection from execution outcomes instead of predicting execution traces. ForeCritic adapts an open 9B typed decision model; held-out pair and agent studies report better selection and reduced runtime, conditional on their task and search protocols.

item.title: Predicting What Answer Engines Cite: Open Decision Models, Rerankers and a Distilled 4B Student on Ten Engines under Controlled Retrieval
item.description: Compares hosted and open decision models, rerankers and distilled students under controlled retrieval. Joint versus single-passage scoring explains much of the student–Jev gap; an insignificant difference does not establish equivalence.

item.title: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG
item.description: Compares eleven hosted decision models on RAG knowledge-conflict typing. Confidence-based escalation can approach a stronger LLM at lower billed cost, while yes/no decomposition hurts accuracy and source-order sensitivity varies across models.

item.title: DFIP: Decision-Focused Inference Path for System One Models
item.description: Audits CUDA replay, candidate projection and length-aware batching in four open decision models. Fixed-workload speedups can disappear or reverse under changing arrivals; preserved labels do not ensure preserved confidence-based routing.

item.title: PsyJev: Psychological Analysis via System-1 Judgment
item.description: Adapts RLCD to heterogeneous question-conditioned judgments through balanced supervision, retention of correct supervised predictions and question-group rewards. Controlled small-model comparisons examine training stages and probability quality on psychological-analysis tasks.

item.title: Learning to Formalize: Bridging Open-Ended Workloads and Fast Decision Models
item.description: Trains a candidate formalizer from offline teacher-generated lists and lets a frozen decision model select a validated action. Separate official-Jev and privileged-state local-model CALVIN studies show strong dependence on candidate construction; their success rates are not a shared head-to-head comparison.

item.title: Confidence Is Not a Promise: A Reference Audit of Typed Decision Models
item.description: Audits selective decisions, calibration transfer, noise, drift and explanations for Laya and Jev 1.13. Point-estimate thresholds often miss promised accuracy; lower-bound qualification helps in exchangeable tests, while language and input shifts break transfer.

item.title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
item.description: Evaluates an open System One model across medical knowledge and patient-level tasks. Good benchmark calibration does not transfer to all patient predictions; a two-parameter local recalibration with 50–200 labels reduces reported calibration error.

item.title: Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?
item.description: Tracks answers across shuffled options and fixed-order repeats. Nearly stable aggregate Jev accuracy masks an expanding set of failed questions, and repeated agreement does not ensure correctness.

item.title: Improving JEV Entailment Reranking with Span Readouts and Selective Adaptation
item.description: Combines mean-span option readouts with selective backbone adapters for entailment reranking. It improves NeoHorse-1-4B reranking with fewer trainable parameters, while gains do not uniformly transfer to direct-decision suites.

item.title: RubriX: A Fast, Fine-Tunable Non-Autoregressive Rubric Judge
item.description: Uses separate encoder representations and cached rubric-level embeddings for non-generative judging. It improves held-out rubric accuracy and keeps latency nearly constant with long level descriptions; human-labelled benchmarks and ranking show mixed advantages over Jev.

item.title: SHIFT-JEV: Certified Abstention and Gain-Gated Continual Adaptation for LLM-Based Decision Models under Distribution Shift
item.description: Combines calibrated abstention, shift monitoring and gain-gated adaptation for open LLM decision models. Calibration improves under shift, but certified thresholds still exceed target risk in some shifted tests and conservative update gates can lose accuracy.

item.title: Decision-Native Recommendation with Large Language Models
item.description: Uses tree-structured attention to share user-history computation across isolated candidate branches. The decision interface tests order-consistent choices, calibrated confidence and selective computation in sequential recommendation.

item.title: Decoupling Calibration, Cross-Sectional Ranking, and Execution in Financial News Models
item.description: Separates probability calibration, directional discrimination and portfolio ranking in financial-news evaluations of Jev and three language models. Low ECE can accompany weak discrimination; different samples and execution windows limit comparisons of predictive and economic usefulness.

item.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to System 1 Models: Fast Decision-Making Beyond LLMS
item.description: Surveys five System 1 model families, their training and deployment trade-offs, calibration and fast–slow cascades. Its taxonomy and ecosystem overview organize existing evidence rather than establish a new controlled comparison.

item.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
item.description: Studies robot-specialized adaptation and calibration transfer of JEV-27B-VL with source-specific KL anchoring. Matched-input tests improve same-robot accuracy but do not establish unseen-domain gains; frontier API comparisons use fewer frames.

item.title: Seeing the Options: Typed Decisions over Visual Candidates with Reusable Option Memory
item.description: Extends typed decisions to visual candidates with reusable option encodings. Request-conditioned independent branches retain candidate-order invariance and improve accuracy over independent encoding, while caching reduces repeated-candidate inference cost.

item.title: Benchmarking System One Models for Time-Series Decision Making: A Case Study of Jev
item.description: Tests Jev 1.13.0 on temporal classification and discretized forecasting. Selected explicit temporal patterns are handled better than many numerical sequences, with near-chance discrimination and gaps between score ranking and final decisions on some datasets.

item.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
item.description: Compares typed decision models, generative LLMs and classical baselines using human-labelled multilingual inbox decisions. Higher field accuracy can produce more missed required actions; cost-aware threshold selection changes the downstream trade-off.

item.title: System One models Are Not Better Rerankers
item.description: Matches six Qwen backbones to compare decision and reranker fine-tuning across ten retrieval collections. Reranker tuning wins through 9B and ties at 27B; decision-model calibration advantages depend on question wording and do not compensate for weaker ranking.

item.title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback
item.description: Stores typed corrections in bounded action and preference-relation channels above a frozen scorer, without extra scorer calls or runtime backpropagation. A chronological benchmark measures effects on later decisions; reported gains depend on prior feedback depth.

item.title: How Well Do Decision Models Transfer to Vietnamese? An Empirical Study of Text Classification
item.description: Evaluates four decision models across 13 Vietnamese classification settings and label-language variants. Removing diacritics causes larger degradation than teencode or typographical errors; bilingual descriptions offer no consistent gain.

item.title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
item.description: Evaluates four System 1 models across 86 medical tasks, 14 domains and 20 languages. Performance and efficiency vary strongly by task and language, including large translation-related losses; benchmark scores do not establish clinical decision reliability.

item.title: One Pretrained Decision Model Is Enough for Training-Free Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection
item.description: Maps structural, attribute and neighborhood anomaly evidence into semantic graph states for a frozen decision readout, fused with statistical scores. Seven graph benchmarks test a training-free approach; reported averages do not establish robustness to adaptive attacks.

item.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
item.description: Studies small typed decision heads for perimeter triage, unknown families and signature cascades. Detection gains coexist with weaker attribution and severe calibration drift; payload-less traffic reconstruction limits cascade interpretation.

item.title: Which Differences Matter? Controlled Tests of Rule Transfer, Joint Reliability, and Information Use in Decision Models
item.description: Uses executable rules, crossed states and controlled rewrites to study transfer and joint correctness. Jev changes answers more across equivalent wordings than identical repeats; conclusions about joint reliability depend on what the calibration reference preserves.

item.title: Commit or Abstain? System One Decision Models, LLMs, and Missing Legal Authority
item.description: Removes correct legal authorities to test abstention alongside standard CaseHOLD accuracy. Decision models can match strong LLM accuracy at lower reported inference cost, yet often still select an authority when none is valid; an agreement gate reduces errors.

item.title: When Multiple Choices Are Correct: Asymmetric Probability Allocation in Jev and Other Decision Models
item.description: Tests probability allocation when several choices are correct: even perfect ranking can place a correct choice below the uniform threshold, and identical choices receive unequal probabilities. Thresholding does not reliably recover the correct set.

item.title: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
item.description: Reports an internal typed judge and open LoRA decision models. Public hard-tier results are single-seed and developed with the evaluation items in view; corpus revisions shift small-benchmark accuracy substantially.

item.title: Scan or Index? large Evidence Coverage, Answer Quality, and Cost in Long-Document RAG
item.description: Compares 11 long-document retrieval configurations with fixed passages, output budget and answer generator. Full scans can lose evidence during reduction; evidence coverage, answer quality and reuse cost favor different configurations.

item.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
item.description: Compares Jev with LLM judges using physician ratings and model-based references across four clinical-output evaluation settings. Agreement and lower measured cost/latency concern the tested judging configurations, not clinical deployment safety.

item.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
item.description: Combines solver-checked contrast groups and public reference tasks across seven decision roles. Evaluating 40 decision models and 14 general models separates joint correctness, probability ordering and selective coverage that aggregate public scores can obscure.

item.title: Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision
item.description: Treats multimodal reranking as a single choice over retrieved candidates; choice readouts outperform per-candidate yes/no scoring, while text-only decision tuning improves document reranking. Cross-model comparisons are confounded by size and generation.

item.title: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models
item.description: Derives exact risks for teacher targets, frozen representations and calibration in Gaussian surrogates; experiments show that better calibration and more student data do not remove inherited teacher bias.

item.title: SOMA: Continuous Monitoring and Intervention for System Two Reasoning with System One Models
item.description: Continuously monitors reasoning with a shared decision model and escalating interventions; reports up to 36% fewer reasoning tokens and higher abstention on unanswerable questions without training.

item.title: Typed Decision Models under Prevalence Shift: Decision Training, Calibration, and Implicit Priors
item.description: Separates decision training from backbone readouts and tests five datasets under label shift; gains are task dependent, and existing miscalibration matters more than unique fragility to shift.

item.title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency
item.description: Learns gated time-series compression and embedding alignment from sufficiency and realizability objectives, enabling single-pass decisions; reports improved performance and lower latency across 13 datasets.

item.title: Claim Laundering: When Agent Decision Models Trust Records Over Reality
item.description: Finds that hosted Jev and open decision models often favor claimed success over contradictory observations in agent decisions. An intermediate-state evidence gate improves open-model live task success, but offline gate calibration transfers poorly.

item.title: A Cue's Hidden Price: Auditing Seller Influence on AI Shoppers
item.description: Measures seller-cue influence as the price premium that equalizes choice probability; 113,472 controlled trials show that Jev resists many cues but remains sensitive to strong social-proof claims.

item.title: UniJev: Separating Accuracy from Calibration in Trimodal System One Decision Models
item.description: Separates supervised accuracy gains from calibration in text, image and video decision models; confidence-outcome alignment lowers visual ECE at 2B and 9B while preserving accuracy without reinforcement learning.

item.title: Truncated Reasoning Under a Budget: Evaluating System-1 Models as Decision-makers
item.description: Evaluates Jev as a reader of truncated reasoning across 35 reasoner-benchmark pairs; a training-fold-selected policy reduces estimated cost with a small held-out accuracy loss in offline replay.

item.title: Narrow Decision Models: A System-1 Architecture for Calibrated, Typed Decisions
item.description: Uses prefix-tree block attention and logical positions to make organization-specific decisions invariant to option order and independent across questions; small-scale validation tests these properties and routing behavior.

item.title: P(Yes): 15$\times$ Improvements via Test-Time Scaling of Decision Models
item.description: Searches candidate answers using frozen models' Yes probabilities, improving logic-puzzle accuracy without training; the headline 15-fold gain is exact correctness from 2 to 30 of 128 puzzles.

item.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
item.description: Adds a text-reply choice and reuses the decision KV cache for generation; measured latency falls, but support-task gains trade off against instruction following and reply preferences depend on the judge.

item.title: What Can't Jev Decide? Probing the Limits of One-Pass Decision Models
item.description: Probes state updates and stale summaries in one-pass decision models; strong record retrieval does not ensure multi-update reasoning, and confidence or handoff options fail to detect inherited state errors.

item.title: Native Probability Outputs for Clinical Triage: An Evaluation of Calibration and Decision Accuracy
item.description: Compares native probabilities and action accuracy on public triage cases; Jev has lower observed Brier scores but weaker action F1 and misses clarification needs, separating calibration from decision quality.

item.title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
item.description: Holds a terminal-agent loop fixed while comparing five controllers; Jev increases cost by 19% at the same observed pass rate, showing that informative completion signals need not yield useful interventions.

item.title: Jarvis: Coordination Deserves a Brain of Its Own in Agentic Interactive Models
item.description: Coordinates live tasks with typed decisions and version checks, revalidating plans and spoken results when requests change; matched front/back models improve voice-task success from 29 to 192 of 278 tasks.

item.title: TUPLE-Bench: Evaluating and Mitigating Privacy-Utility Trade-offs in Typed Decision Models
item.description: Audits leakage through selected categories, option scores and confidence across nine decision models; workflow-constrained quantization reduces secret recovery while preserving specified downstream actions and costs.

item.title: Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking
item.description: Compares Jev relevance judgments with official labels in four Portuguese retrieval collections; moderate item-level agreement can coexist with similar system rankings, and BM25 reranking improves in the tested setting.

item.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
item.description: Trains Chinese single-pass decision models using candidate-letter logits and distribution targets; the completed 0.8B model reports 1.07% calibration error, while partial 2B training does not isolate a scale effect.

item.title: Literal Lock-In: How Test Language Shifts Literal Attraction in Typed Decision Models on Bengali Idioms
item.description: Compares Laya, Lod-lille and Jev on paired Bengali idiom questions and English glosses. Literal distractors dominate Bengali errors, calibration worsens, and confidence reverses its usefulness for the two open models.

item.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
item.description: Uses masked decision placeholders in a JSON skeleton for one-pass multimodal choices; reports compact-model accuracy, latency and small calibration and handoff pilots.

item.title: Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models
item.description: Isolates option scoring in shared-position attention blocks to enforce order and rival independence; reports near-baseline accuracy with stable choices under tested option changes.

item.title: Qwen-Audio-Jev: A Unified Interface for Audio Decisions
item.description: Adds typed CHOICE, NOUL and SCORE readouts to an audio backbone; reports results across 18 labeled configurations and about 20-fold inference speedup over its generative backbone.

item.title: JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs
item.description: Fits delegation thresholds on agent trajectories and trains a 4B decision model on reached states; shows that isolated-question accuracy does not predict closed-loop agent success.

item.title: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows
item.description: Separates expert routing and artifact screening from generative execution and feedback; reports 12.7–54.6% fewer generative tokens with accuracy within 1.34 points of LAS.

item.title: System1-Arena: Which Decisions Can Be Left to System 1?
item.description: Benchmarks probabilities on 92k questions and 138 closed-loop environments; strong static decision accuracy does not translate uniformly into agent success.

item.title: Prune the Summary, Not the History: Source-Judged Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: Uses Jev to remove summary entries lacking support in environment outputs or prior summaries; reports improved cross-run reliability on AppWorld and OfficeBench.

item.title: From Detection to Decision: Calibration and Deferral for Prompt-Injection Detection
item.description: Evaluates detection, calibration and allow-block-defer policies on 47,611 held-out examples; native Jev probabilities do not consistently outperform calibrated classifiers and low-FNR operation requires extensive escalation.

item.title: Verdict: Encode Once, Decide Many
item.description: Shares a question-independent state encoding across typed questions with option invariance; improves agreement with soft labels but exposes accuracy–latency costs of removing question-aware state encoding.

item.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
item.description: Evaluates 180 live-clock tasks and teaches a fast student between attempts with a slow teacher; reports Jev test-score improvement from 13.51 to 24.19 after two rounds.

item.title: Diagnose Before You Refine: Multi-Dimensional Judge Feedback for Query-Efficient Jailbreak Attacks
item.description: Uses multidimensional probabilistic judge feedback to guide query-budgeted jailbreak optimization and evaluates target-query efficiency and output filtering.

item.title: Lost in the Fallback: How Reliably Do Typed Decision Models Use Fallback Options?
item.description: Tests regular-to-fallback switching and equivalent fallback definitions; correct category recognition does not reliably yield correct fallback execution.

item.title: Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models
item.description: Uses Learn Then Test to select utility actions under a risk budget and conservative fallback; reports fewer target-risk violations than naive threshold selection across six datasets.

item.title: Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop
item.description: Combines a candidate reader with reasoning-start, read and stop policies; measures accuracy, generated work and pipeline time under matched-prefix controls.

item.title: Are AI Decision Models Biased? A Case Study of Jev
item.description: Tests cognitive and demographic biases and extends conjunction tasks; stable selected answers can conceal probability shifts, numerical anchoring and option-order sensitivity.

item.title: JevCoder: When Does Decision Delegation Pay Off in Code Repair?
item.description: Studies which code-repair decisions benefit from delegation; on 400 shared tasks, the reported Jev workflow reduces repair-model token use while improving observed repair rates.

item.title: Typed Decision Models on Tabular Data
item.description: Compares decision models and LLMs under 21 content-preserving table and question rewrites; lower-cost typed decisions remain sensitive to table organization.

item.title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision
item.description: Benchmarks text and visual attacks with held-out target models; robustness varies by task and attack, and label-consistency checks reduce apparent attack success.

item.title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: Audits source-to-decision handoffs with Jev to distinguish error introduction, propagation and repair; improves failure-step localization on five multi-agent benchmark subsets.

item.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
item.description: Introduces a decision architecture with independent option encoding, symmetric aggregation and separate coverage estimation to support permutation invariance, null outcomes and cached reuse.

item.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
item.description: Uses shared decision heads and reusable visual computation for temporal grounding and video QA; the authors report faster inference with comparable or improved task scores.

item.title: Nudge the Judge: Uncovering Program Decision Hijacking in Real-World Jev Applications
item.description: Traces attacker-controlled context to program-consumed decisions in Jev applications. The released benchmark has 81.5% flips in a flips-first curated subset; its impact labels describe potential consequences, not observed real-world harm.

item.title: Jev-ToM: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Typed Decision Models
item.description: Evaluates typed models on 11,117 theory-of-mind questions; Jev leads several capabilities, while confidence filtering, supplied reasons and candidate expansion remain task-dependent.

item.title: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops
item.description: Pairs action choices with factual probes across agent states; most wrong actions follow correct reading, exposing failures of composition and sub-goal selection.

item.title: How Reliable Are System-One Decisions in Medicine? A Comparative Study of Jev, Jev-like Models, and LLMs
item.description: Tests accuracy, prompt stability and abstention across 15 medical datasets; Jev is stronger on text than numerical tasks, while recognizing missing answers remains difficult.

item.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments
item.description: Candidate-blind reference generation improves tool-argument verification, including hosted Jev, across three benchmarks. Judges also follow incorrect references, so gains rely on reference quality and require an extra derivation model.

item.title: Recalibrating Many Questions with Few Labels: Minimax Rates and Identification Limits
item.description: Derives minimax rates and identification limits for recalibrating related questions, with pooled isotonic fitting and held-out corrections under monotone calibration-map assumptions.

item.title: PRISM: Calibrating Black-Box Judges with Counterfactual Probes
item.description: Uses counterfactual scoring probes and human-label regression to correct black-box judges; improves reported human-ranking agreement on summarization and story evaluation.

item.title: Jev-Guard: Fast Routing and Auditing Agent Actions over Editable Policy Trees
item.description: Routes audit contexts through editable policy trees and performs policy-conditioned safety classification; evaluates both standalone routing and agent permission gating.

item.title: Consider, Then Choose: Order-Invariant Decisions in System One Models
item.description: Combines independent option scoring with position-balanced runoff comparisons to remove option-order dependence; compares accuracy and inference cost against cyclic averaging.

item.title: Cheap, Consistent, Calibrated, but Biased? Typed Decision Models as Judges
item.description: Tests eight typed models on twelve CALM biases; calibration and consistency coexist with emotional-tone, position and attribution biases in pairwise judging.

item.title: Same Attack, Different Judge: A First Controlled Adversarial Comparison of Jev, LLM Judges, and Purpose-Built Safety Classifiers
item.description: Compares matched adversarial payloads across Jev, LLM judges and safety classifiers; Jev resists rule-based moderation attacks better than phishing attacks and has substantial benign false positives.

item.title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions
item.description: Combines single-pass Instant models with confidence-guided AutoThink reasoning; calibrated deliberative reinforcement learning reduces reasoning length while preserving reported accuracy.

item.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models
item.description: Reads option-letter logits from instruction-tuned LMs and improves them with LoRA decision-head tuning; evaluates accuracy and calibration on OpenDecisions and JevBench.

item.title: FunDM: Cheap & Label-Free Decision Models from Frozen Language Models
item.description: Distills frozen language-model probabilities into small decision heads without correctness labels, retaining most multiple-choice accuracy with fewer transformer layers.

item.title: ProbabilityBench: Model Evaluation and Calibration with Exact Ground-Truth Uncertainty
item.description: Defines simulated text tasks with exact conditional probabilities and Bayes error, enabling direct probability-quality evaluation and meta-evaluation of calibration metrics.

item.title: Proactive Physical AI through Continuous Observation and Timely Intervention
item.description: Introduces a Jev-style timing model that separates intervention decisions from response generation, with video-derived supervision for continuous physical-world observation.

item.title: Does a Hosted Decision Model Respect Irrelevant Alternatives? A Pre-Registered Test of Option-Set Dependence in Jev
item.description: Across 299,463 calls, adding low-probability alternatives shifts Jev's relative odds; independent binary scoring removes set dependence at an accuracy cost.

item.title: Correct Choices, Failed Sequences: Choice2Seq Benchmarks Correctness Retention Across Output Interfaces
item.description: Measures how often correct complete-answer selections survive sequential construction; Jev's high arithmetic and lexical selection accuracy can collapse under serial output interfaces.

item.title: Jev, OpenAI, AWS, Perplexity: Do Decision Models Know When They're Wrong?: A pre-registered test of the calibration and accuracy of seven decision models on the same 799 unpublished yes/no decisions
item.description: Reuses the same 799-item bank with fresh Jev calls to compare seven decision models; only the reported Perplexity checkpoint has its full ECE interval below the study threshold.

item.title: RSAJEV: Training-Free Abstaining Prototype Memory for Eliminating Silent Hallucination in JEV-Based Remote Sensing Classification
item.description: Replaces letter-token readout with cached prototype retrieval to improve cross-dataset classification and open-set abstention in Jev-style remote-sensing models.

item.title: Suggested Is Not Superseded: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of a System-One Model as a Memory-Retirement Gate
item.description: Separates established memory changes from suggestions; a three-way Jev gate reduces premature retirement but exceeds its preregistered detection-loss budget.

item.title: Poisoned into Action: Context Attacks on Typed Decision Workflows
item.description: Traces poisoned context through retrieval, typed decisions and persisted state; defenses trade prevented violations against withheld correct automation in two synthetic workflows.

item.title: Jev: Twenty Times Faster, Seven Points Behind: Does Jev know when it is wrong? A pre-registered test of a decision model's calibration and accuracy beside two general-purpose models
item.description: On 799 coding-agent and command-safety items, Jev trails two general-purpose models in paired accuracy; its calibration interval crosses the study-defined ECE threshold.

item.title: A Thermometer, Not an Analyst: Lawful Uses of a Text Judge in a Live Trading Lab
item.description: Studies six checks for a version-pinned Jev headline judge, including repeatability, time context and simple baselines; reports weak or disappearing signals and post-failure infrastructure corrections, without testing trading-return improvement.

item.title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
item.description: Across 4,500 agent executions, Jev lowers decision costs and latency, but mobile-agent success losses and recovery overhead can offset savings per delivered outcome.

item.title: One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails
item.description: Separates fail-open and fail-closed errors in open decision-model guardrails; misleading option names can reverse decisions when labels enter the model input.

item.title: Specialized Decision Models vs. General-Purpose LLMs: Benchmarking Jev Across Knowledge, Reasoning, and Multilingual Tasks
item.description: Compares Jev with 19 LLMs on 13 benchmarks; strong knowledge scores coexist with a marked weakness on mathematical word problems.

item.title: Can Decision Models Understand Stance? Evaluating Jev Against General-Purpose LLMs
item.description: Jev matches GPT-5.6 on English VAST stance labels but trails stronger models on Chinese conversational stance, especially favor-versus-against distinctions.

item.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
item.description: Uses frozen Jev as a policy reference, exploration judge and replay rater; gains depend on the learning role and supplied information.

item.title: Adversarial Cues in Decision Models Used as Judges: The Role of Request Presentation
item.description: A colon edit increases false acceptance of explicitly wrong final answers under sorted request keys, while insertion-order requests reject both variants.

item.title: TypedBench: A Benchmark for Calibration, Framing Sensitivity, and Cost in System One Decision Models
item.description: Uses policy-driven generators to test calibration, framing, abstention and cost; good error ranking does not ensure calibrated or evidence-sensitive confidence.

item.title: FastJEV: Understanding Redundancy for Compact JEV Inference
item.description: Combines context-state reuse, candidate-prefix sharing and layer pruning for OmniJev; compact execution does not consistently reduce measured latency.

item.title: MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface
item.description: Trains a multimodal bi-encoder with request-to-candidate contrastive learning; including options in requests improves closed-set decisions while retaining cached candidate embeddings.

item.title: Can a System-One LLM Perform Knowledge Tracing When Few or No Learners Are Logged?
item.description: Tests cold-start knowledge tracing with reader swaps and matched typed inputs; Jev benefits mainly from its model prior, while supervised methods catch up with more learners.

item.title: JevForest: Path Voting for Budgeted Feature Acquisition
item.description: Uses tree-path voting to select semantic questions under a feature budget; fewer sequential questions cost more than batching in the tested pilots.

item.title: Where Can a Decision Model Diagnose HVAC Faults? Reasoning Demand, Physical Representation, and Robustness Under Shift
item.description: Separates physical representation from reasoning in fault diagnosis; engineered features improve consistency, but stable shift performance does not imply superior absolute accuracy or useful detection.

item.title: System Switch: When Should a Fast Decision Model Stop and Think?
item.description: Tests confidence-based deferral from fast decision models to a slow visual reasoner; offline gains do not translate into Doom level completion.

item.title: Visual Jev Rewards: Reference-Bound Verification for Multi-Subject Image Generation
item.description: Trains a local Qwen verifier for joint reference identity and image conditions, then averages binary probabilities as an image-generation reward.

item.title: Calibrated Decisions Are Not Calibrated Probabilities: An Exact-Target Audit of Jev and Three Open Decision Models
item.description: Audits exact probability targets and human disagreement: normalized Noul better tracks stated base rates, while per-task calibration narrows the gap on human-vote distributions.

item.title: From Probabilities to Decisions: Search and Multi-Teacher Distillation with Jev
item.description: Distills Jev and Qwen pairwise probabilities into small evaluators; matched-budget chess gains replicate, while retrieval gains remain uncertain.

item.title: Agent in a Bottle: Can LLM Agents Turn Their Capabilities Into Cheap, Scalable Artifacts?
item.description: Benchmarks agents that build reusable artifacts for large workloads; most runs lose quality relative to zero-shot calls, while selected artifacts approach Jev at lower projected API cost.

item.title: Same-Number Citation Swaps: Stress-Testing Jev as a Financial Evidence Judge
